name: task and lease endpoints use half-open TTL intervals
input: a task with an eight-unit lifetime and a three-unit lease
test:
manager = SnapshotTaskManager()
manager.create('email', 'send receipt', 10, 8)
assert manager.ready(10) == ['email']
assert manager.claim('email', 'worker-a', 11, 3) is True
assert manager.ready(13) == []
assert manager.ready(14) == ['email']
assert manager.get('email', 17) == {'task_id': 'email', 'payload': 'send receipt', 'status': 'ready', 'worker': None}
assert manager.get('email', 18) is None
assert manager.claim('email', 'worker-b', 18, 1) is False

name: only the current lease holder can finish a live task
input: a leased task, wrong worker, expired lease, and new worker
test:
manager = SnapshotTaskManager()
manager.create('cleanup', 'remove temp files', 0, 20)
assert manager.claim('cleanup', 'a', 2, 3) is True
assert manager.finish('cleanup', 'b', 3) is False
assert manager.finish('cleanup', 'a', 5) is False
assert manager.claim('cleanup', 'b', 5, 4) is True
assert manager.finish('cleanup', 'b', 8) is True
assert manager.get('cleanup', 8) is None
assert manager.ready(8) == []

name: snapshots preserve remaining task and lease time independently
input: two tasks, one leased at snapshot time, then restore at a later time
test:
manager = SnapshotTaskManager()
manager.create('alpha', 'index docs', 5, 10)
manager.create('beta', 'send digest', 0, 20)
assert manager.claim('alpha', 'worker-a', 6, 7) is True
snapshot = manager.snapshot(10)
assert manager.finish('beta', 'nobody', 11) is False
assert manager.claim('beta', 'worker-b', 11, 4) is True
assert manager.finish('beta', 'worker-b', 12) is True
manager.restore(snapshot, 30)
assert manager.get('alpha', 32)['status'] == 'leased'
assert manager.get('alpha', 32)['worker'] == 'worker-a'
assert manager.ready(33) == ['alpha', 'beta']
assert manager.get('alpha', 35) is None
assert manager.get('beta', 39) == {'task_id': 'beta', 'payload': 'send digest', 'status': 'ready', 'worker': None}
assert manager.get('beta', 40) is None

name: snapshots and reads do not expose mutable internal state
input: a snapshot and read result that callers mutate
test:
manager = SnapshotTaskManager()
manager.create('one', 'payload', 0, 5)
snapshot = manager.snapshot(1)
snapshot['tasks']['one']['payload'] = 'tampered'
assert manager.get('one', 1)['payload'] == 'payload'
view = manager.get('one', 1)
view['payload'] = 'changed'
assert manager.get('one', 1)['payload'] == 'payload'
for call in (lambda: manager.create('', 'x', 0, 1), lambda: manager.create('x', '', 0, 1), lambda: manager.create('x', 'y', -1, 1), lambda: manager.create('x', 'y', 0, 0), lambda: manager.claim('one', '', 1, 1)):
    try:
        call()
        raise AssertionError('expected ValueError')
    except ValueError:
        pass
